# Agent Rules Library

> **📋 DOCUMENTATION RULES FOR AI ASSISTANTS**
>
> **Document Type**: Tier 2 Reference Document (Template)
> **Purpose**: Opinionated, technology-specific rules collected from real projects, to copy into a project's `AGENTS.md`
> **Update Frequency**: When a project produces a rule worth reusing
>
> **When editing this document**:
> - ✅ Group rules by technology, and keep each rule's original meaning
> - ✅ Write rules as plain sentences - emphasis follows the bar in `AGENTS.md` → "Emphasis"
> - ✅ Mark project-specific values (profiles, paths, decision IDs) so they are adjusted when copied
> - ❌ Don't follow these rules unless they have been copied into the project's `AGENTS.md`
> - ❌ Don't add generic rules that already live in the `AGENTS.md` template
>
> **Full Documentation System**: [docs/00_ONBOARDING.md](../00_ONBOARDING.md)

**How to use:** copy the sections that match your stack into "Project-Specific Rules" in `AGENTS.md`, then adjust the values marked *(adjust)*.

---

## Agent Habits

- An empty result isn't evidence of absence. Before reading "not found" as "not there", search the same target for something you know is present. Blanks that looked like answers have come from a grep that refused its own pattern and printed nothing, a search of a file that never held the code (the bundler had moved it into another chunk), and a CLI query that returned empty for a commit whose results existed.
- Don't trust a status or a silence you didn't verify. In a pipeline, the exit status is the last command's: `run-tests | tee log` reports success when the tests fail, unless `set -o pipefail` is on.
- Two implementations of one operation drift apart. When one already exists, delete the duplicate rather than extend it, and collapse duplicates before adding new behaviour, not after.
- A rendered view of a document - an HTML page drawn from a Markdown source - is generated by a script that has `--check`, and is never edited by hand. Two hand-kept copies of the same journeys, one Markdown and one HTML, drifted apart. Run the check in the test script so a stale view fails CI.
- *(For teams that don't want agent memory files)* Don't save agent memory files. Anything a later session must know goes in `AGENTS.md`, the session document, or the design doc that owns it - where every person and every agent reads it.

## Editing Files

- Edit by exact string match, never by offset arithmetic. Use an edit tool with a unique `old_string`, or a scripted replace of an exact literal. Don't compute a start and end with `str.index()` and splice: searching for the next `\ndef ` to find where one helper ended skipped past decorated `async def` handlers, matched 819 lines later, and deleted 13 routes. If a replacement must span a region, print the region first and match its real first and last lines.
- After any scripted edit, run `git diff --stat` before anything else. A surprising line count is the cheapest way to catch a bad splice.

## Shell & Local Environment

- We use zsh for the shell.
- zsh aborts a command on an unmatched glob, where bash passes the pattern through. Quote glob patterns, including those passed as flag values (`--include='*.ts'`, `git ls-files '*.md'`). Otherwise a pattern that matches nothing kills the command with "no matches found", which reads like a broken tool instead of an empty result. For `rm` it's worse: `rm -f a b dir/*.orig` aborts before removing anything, and the files that did exist stay behind - remove them in separate commands, or check the glob matches first.
- In zsh, brace a variable that a colon follows: `"${ACCT}:log-group"`, not `"$ACCT:log-group"`. After a variable, `:l`, `:u`, `:r`, `:h` and `:t` are modifiers - lowercase, uppercase, strip an extension, the head, the tail - so the unbraced form silently drops or changes characters. It wrote a malformed IAM policy ARN and a broken git refspec, with no error where the mistake was made.
- In zsh, don't name a variable `path` - it is tied to `$PATH`, so `for path in ...` wipes it and every command after it fails with "command not found".

## Git

- Move and rename files with `git mv`, never copy and delete. It keeps history and stages the change in one step.
- `gh pr merge --delete-branch` is unsafe while another open PR targets that branch. Deleting the base auto-closes the dependent PR, and a later force-push to its head makes reopening it impossible. Retarget the dependent PR to `main` first.
- When a branch moved code, a conflict in the moved region is a fix to re-apply at its new address, not a formatting conflict. Resolving it as "ours" compiles, passes every test, and silently restores the bug that was fixed on `main`.
- A `git diff` taken while a code generator is running shows half-written files as huge deletions. Wait for the generator to finish before reading it.
- `gh` signs in through this project's own configuration directory - `GH_CONFIG_DIR` in `.claude/settings.local.json` ([Git Identities](../guides/MULTI-IDENTITY-GIT-SSH-SETUP-GUIDE.md#7-the-github-cli-one-account-per-project)). Never run `gh auth switch`: the active account is shared by every project using that directory. Sign a directory in with `gh auth login --insecure-storage`: a plain login replaces the keychain token every directory shares. Check the account gh acts as with `gh api user --jq .login` - `gh auth status` reads the configuration, not the token - and `echo $GH_CONFIG_DIR` before assuming GitHub is at fault.
- `gh pr checks --watch` started right after a push can report the previous commit's results, before the new runs register. Before merging on green checks, confirm they ran on the pull request's head commit (`gh pr view --json headRefOid,statusCheckRollup`) or that its `mergeable_state` is clean.

## Secrets

- Never ask the owner to paste a key, token or password into the session, or to run a command that prints one through the `!` prefix: both put it in the transcript. Give the command for their own terminal - one that reads the secret from a prompt or a file - then verify the secret by name only, such as `gh secret list` or `aws secretsmanager describe-secret`.

### Shared Working Tree

Another agent session may be working in this same checkout, and it can switch branches between your `git add` and your `git commit`.

- Commit from an isolated `git worktree` whenever another session may be active: `git worktree add <path> -b tmp/<name> origin/main`, commit there, `git push origin HEAD:main`, then remove the worktree.
- After committing, check `git log --oneline -1` to see where the commit landed. Don't assume.
- In a shared tree, never run `git reset --hard` or `git stash` - that is someone else's uncommitted work. Stage only your own hunks (filter the patch and use `git apply --cached`), and compare `git status --porcelain` before and after any recovery to prove their work is untouched.

## Testing

- A green local lint doesn't mean CI is green when the local image caches tool versions and CI installs them fresh. The newer release enforces rules the cached one doesn't (import sorting is the usual one). Believe CI, and rebuild the image rather than assuming CI is wrong. Better still, pin tool versions in one file that both read.
- Give each worktree its own Docker test environment: derive the Compose project name and image tag from the worktree path, and never hardcode `-p <name>` in a script or a doc. A shared project fails in both directions at once: one run sees missing tables or exit 137, while the other prints a clean "N passed" that belongs to the other branch. Four things collide - the project name, a fixed `container_name`, a fixed host port and a shared image tag - and fixing fewer than all four doesn't work.

## Product Specs and Scenarios

- Every behaviour a scenario shows uses an existing UI element type and an operation the app already has, and names where it lives - a rule in code, a field a model already outputs, or judgment in a prompt *(adjust: cite the decision that sets this)*.
- Test a scenario with one case and with ten. A layout that looked fine with one item had no answer for ten.
- If a scenario needs something new - an element type, a model output field, a rule - raise it in the spec or as a key decision first, and list what is missing under Open questions. Never draw it into a scenario first.
- A change to a rule a scenario shows updates the scenarios in the same change, and regenerates any rendered view *(adjust: the render script)*.

## AWS

- Connect to AWS CLI using this profile: --profile my-aws-profile *(adjust)*

## AWS Lambda & SAM

- All Lambdas use container deployment (`PackageType: Image`). Don't use `CodeUri`/`Handler`/`Runtime`: ZIP deployment breaks Python imports.
- Each Lambda has `Metadata` (`Dockerfile`, `DockerContext`), `PackageType: Image` and `ImageConfig`.
- See DECISION_013 in docs/05_DESIGN-DECISIONS.md *(adjust: record the matching decision)*
- Run `./scripts/sam-validate.sh` before pushing to catch template errors.
- When working on Lambdas in Docker, build for x86_64 even on an ARM64 Mac, using emulation. GitHub Actions builds x86_64, and building ARM there is far too slow.

## Local Backend (Docker)

- Start the local backend only with `./scripts/start-backend.sh` *(adjust)*, never `docker start`, `docker restart` or Docker Desktop's restart-on-boot. Environment variables are fixed when a container is created, so a restarted container silently keeps the old ones; the script migrates first and lets `docker compose up` recreate changed containers. See `docs/guides/LOCAL-BACKEND-GUIDE.md`.
- When a local error looks impossible - a missing column that exists in the models, a flag that does nothing - suspect a stale stack before the code: restart with the script, then re-read the error.
- Put a setting on the service that reads it. A worker's flag set on the API does nothing, and nothing fails.
- Local workers consume from per-developer queues (`localdev-<name>` *(adjust)*). Never point a local worker at a deployed environment's queue: it splits that queue's messages with the deployed consumer.

## LLMs, Prompts, Bedrock & Agents

- On AWS Bedrock, call Anthropic models through inference profiles, not model IDs. Model IDs are fine for models that have no inference profile.
- **A prompt change is a model change: run the evals.** After editing a production prompt, run the eval suite for that task (e.g. `./scripts/run-model-eval.sh --task <task>` *(adjust)*) and confirm its go/no-go gates still pass. If the change targets behaviour the eval corpus doesn't exercise, add fixtures for it first - otherwise the eval is blind to exactly what you changed.
- Write prompt rules for the shape of a situation, never for one example's contents. A fix that copied a worked example straight from an eval case fixed its target and broke an unrelated case; rewritten generically, it fixed both.
- **Don't change a worker's LLM model (Bedrock profile or model ID) without analysis first.** A swap can silently break a use case or balloon cost. Before changing any model: (1) run the eval suite against the task's labeled corpus and confirm its go/no-go gates, (2) confirm the new model supports the modality the worker needs, and does the task rather than only accepting the input - one vision model captioned images when the task needed them transcribed, (3) record the rationale and eval evidence in a decision. Keep model choices in one place *(adjust: e.g. `model_registry.py`)*.
- Deployed prod CloudFormation stack parameters can drift from `template.yaml` defaults - the deploy pipeline doesn't re-pass the `Bedrock*Profile` parameters. Check what prod is actually running (`aws cloudformation describe-stacks`, or the live Lambda environment) before assuming the template default is live.
- When developing agents, use the Strands Agents SDK with Bedrock, not Anthropic's Claude SDK. Bedrock's Converse API is fine for simple interactions with an LLM.

## DynamoDB

- DynamoDB doesn't support float types. Use `Decimal` instead. Store tests that use in-memory mocks instead of a real `put_item` won't catch raw-float writes, so convert floats to `Decimal` at the write boundary with a recursive sanitizer for nested dicts and lists, and unit-test the sanitizer directly.
- `ExpressionAttributeNames` values can't contain dots. For nested attributes, nest the placeholder names.

## Relational Databases & Migrations

- Change the database only through migrations, and run them when needed.
- Make migrations idempotent where possible.

## Frontend (Generated API Client)

- **Never write an API call by hand in the web app.** Call the API through the client generated into `src/app/api/`, which is rebuilt from `openapi.json` before every build and test and is never committed or edited. No `HttpClient` or `httpResource` outside it; `scripts/check-generated-clients.sh` fails the build on one. See `docs/guides/SDK-GENERATION-GUIDE.md`.
- **Don't edit `openapi.json` by hand.** Change the API's code, re-export with `scripts/export-openapi.py` in the backend's Docker image, and commit the spec with the change. Exported on the host, another FastAPI or Pydantic version rewrites half the file.

## iOS, Swift & Xcode

- Tests are Swift/XCTest and run with `xcodebuild` on the Mac, not in Docker: this is the exception to "Run tests in Docker". Run them with `scripts/run-tests.sh` *(adjust)*, which the pre-push hook also runs. See `docs/guides/IOS-TESTING-GUIDE.md`.
- Keep `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` in every test command. Without signing, the test host has no Keychain entitlement and Keychain reads throw, so a suite that passes signed in Xcode can fail in the hook.
- Don't add `-only-testing:<AppTests>` to the standard test run. The scheme's test action holds every bundle, including the extension's *(adjust)*, and narrowing it silently drops them.
- The project uses Xcode 16+ synchronized folder groups: files are included by their folder, not listed in `project.pbxproj`. Don't add files to `project.pbxproj` by hand. Anything left in a target's folder ships inside the app, including Markdown, so keep docs in `docs/`.
- Types re-declared in both the app and an extension are an unchecked wire contract when both sides write the same Keychain item or App Group data. Change both declarations together, and keep a key-set test in each target's bundle.
- `MARKETING_VERSION` is edited by hand in several places *(adjust: list them)*. Bump all of them together, and bump before the first build after a version is approved: App Store Connect closes that version's train.
- Deploys to TestFlight and the App Store are manual workflow dispatches. Merging to `main` doesn't ship anything.
- The API client is hand-written - the one exception to generating clients - and checked: add a model or an operation only with its contract test, and keep `contract/openapi.snapshot.json` from production's spec (`scripts/check-openapi-drift.sh --update`). Every enum is a `LenientEnum`. See `docs/guides/SDK-GENERATION-GUIDE.md`.

## Angular

- Never put a backtick inside an Angular inline template, including in an HTML comment. The template is a TypeScript template literal, so a backtick ends it early and the compiler reports a wall of `TS1005` / `TS1109` / `TS2559` errors pointing at markup that is fine. Write paths, identifiers and attribute names bare in template comments; code-quoting even a bare attribute name breaks the build. Backticks are fine in the class doc comment above the decorator, which is where a code reference usually belongs.
